takeaway: IMPRESS reuses only query-relevant prefix KVs, clustering them on disk and caching chunks by important-content density to reduce LLM time to first token.
background: LLM servers can avoid recomputing shared prompt prefixes by storing their key/value tensors across GPU memory, CPU memory, and SSD. At scale, loading a long prefix from slower tiers can cost more than recomputation, making storage I/O the prefill bottleneck.
villain: Existing KV-pruning methods must first load all keys to discover important tokens, and static importance misses query-dependent context. Chunking then reads unrelated KVs, while LRU/LFU policies favor frequently accessed chunks regardless of how many useful tensors they contain.
approach: IMPRESS observes that important token indices are similar across attention heads in a layer, so it samples probe-head keys to identify them with less I/O. It reorders KVs within radix-tree nodes to pack important tensors into fewer chunks, then manages exclusive GPU/CPU caches with a score combining access frequency and important-KV ratio.
impact: The system connects model attention structure to multi-tier storage placement, making selective prefix reuse beneficial even when most KVs live on SSD. Its techniques complement scheduling, quantization, and finer-grained prefix matching.

evaluation.overview: Three OPT sizes and four few-shot datasets evaluate accuracy, average and p99 time to first token, I/O time, technique contributions, cache behavior, and sensitivity to thresholds, chunk size, dataset size, and Llama models.
evaluation.implemented: A FlexGen-based prototype with modified attention, per-layer reordered KV storage, radix-tree metadata, and a score-managed TokenCache.
evaluation.setting: A dual-64-core EPYC server with 128 GB DRAM, one 80 GB A100, a 2 TB roughly 5 GB/s SSD, 10 GB GPU KV cache and 32 GB CPU KV cache; average prefixes contain 4.8K–5.7K tokens.

results.text: Across four datasets and three OPT models, IMPRESS reports 1.2–2.8× lower average time to first token than the leading alternatives, driven by 1.5–3.8× lower prefix-KV I/O time.
At the chosen retention ratios, average accuracy is 0.2% below recomputation; for OPT-30B on RTE, reported p99 TTFT is 2.95 s versus 3.9–9.3 s for baselines.
KV reordering reduces loaded chunks by 1.2× on average, and importance-scored caching raises average GPU hit ratio from 68% to 80%.

limitations: Because no open real-world prefix-reuse trace was available, the evaluation synthesizes shared prefixes by prepending few-shot examples with normally distributed reuse. AttentionStore is reimplemented and scheduler optimizations are disabled. The core cross-head-similarity observation is empirical rather than universal, and selective KV retention deliberately accepts small quality changes.
phd_group_signal: IMPRESS is an example of ML-systems co-design: it turns a measured model property into an I/O-reduction mechanism, then changes disk layout and cache policy to preserve that benefit. Its evaluation reports both system latency and model quality, which is essential for this class of optimization.

claims.text: IMPRESS loads keys from selected probe heads and uses cross-head similarity to infer important token indices for the remaining heads in each layer.
Within each radix-tree node, KVs are reordered by importance and accompanied by an inverse token mapping, increasing useful-KV density without mixing unshared prefix branches.
